title: Uniform derived Hom bounds from a bounded injective target
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and work in the ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix integers $a\leq b$, a cochain complex $J$ of injective $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-sp-injective-resolutions] satisfying $J^i=0$ for $i<a$ and $i>b$, and an isomorphism $J\cong L$ in $D(R)$. Use derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site and the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every $K\in D(R)$ and every integer $c$, both of the following hold. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i>c$, there is a representative $P\cong K$ with $P^p=0$ for $p>c$, an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_R(P,J)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$ in $D(R)$, and $\operatorname{Hom}^{n}_R(P,J)=0$ for $n<a-c$; hence $H^n(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L))=0$ for $n<a-c$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i<c$, there is a representative $Q\cong K$ with $Q^p=0$ for $p<c$, an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_R(Q,J)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$ in $D(R)$, and $\operatorname{Hom}^{n}_R(Q,J)=0$ for $n>b-c$; hence $H^n(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L))=0$ for $n>b-c$. The integers $a,b$ are fixed independently of $K,c$; no Noetherianity or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] to $J$ in the abelian category of $R$-modules, with lower bound $a$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed injectivity of every $J^i$ and $J^i=0$ for $i<a$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,J)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $A$ of $R$-modules; the upper bound $b$ is not needed for this step. This is K-injectivity in the sense of [def-pur-kinjective-complex] on the one-object site of Step 3: a degree-$0$ cocycle of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,J)$ is a family $f^p:A^p\to J^p$ with $d_Jf=fd_A$, i.e. a morphism of complexes, and the coboundary of a degree-$(-1)$ family $h=(h^p:A^p\to J^{p-1})$ is $d_Jh+hd_A$, so $H^0(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,J))=0$ says exactly that every morphism of complexes $A\to J$ is homotopic to zero.

Choose any complex $C$ representing $K$. For the upper-cohomology hypothesis take $P=\tau_{\le c}C$: its terms are $C^p$ for $p<c$, $\ker d_C^c$ at $c$, and zero above $c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $P\to C$ induces isomorphisms below and at $c$, and above $c$ both cohomologies vanish by hypothesis, so it is a quasi-isomorphism and $P\cong K$. For the lower-cohomology hypothesis take the lower good truncation $Q=\tau_{\ge c}C$ of [def-kun-truncations]: zero below $c$, $C^c/\operatorname{im}d_C^{c-1}$ at $c$, and $C^p$ above $c$. The quotient map $C\to Q$ induces the identity on cohomology above $c$, and at $c$ its cycles are $\ker d_C^c/\operatorname{im}d_C^{c-1}=H^c(C)$ with no incoming boundaries. Below $c$ both cohomologies are zero. Hence this map too is a quasi-isomorphism, so $Q\cong K$. Here quasi-isomorphisms become isomorphisms by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncations in both directions.

proof.text: For either representative $T=P$ or $T=Q$ constructed in its respective case, the K-injective target $J$ represents $L$, so the arbitrary-K-injective-representative clause of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_R(T,J)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$ in $D(R)$. This clause uses the quasi-isomorphism invariance of [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], which is cited explicitly here. Apply these statements on the one-object site with trivial topology and coefficient ring $R$: its module sheaves are exactly $R$-modules, its products and sheaf Hom are the ordinary products and module Hom, and its complexes and quasi-isomorphisms are the ordinary ones. Thus the resulting comparison is an isomorphism of derived $R$-modules, not merely an identification of their cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom, and Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, specialized to the one-object ringed site.

proof.text: In the upper-cohomology case, [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $\operatorname{Hom}^n_R(P,J)=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^p,J^{p+n})$. If $n<a-c$, then for $p\le c$ we have $p+n\le c+n<a$, whence $J^{p+n}=0$; for $p>c$ we have $P^p=0$. Every factor is therefore the zero module, since a linear map from or to zero is zero. Their product is zero: its only element is the family of zero maps. This proves the requested termwise vanishing. Since the degree-$n$ term is zero, its kernel modulo its incoming image is zero, so the comparison in Step 3 gives $H^n(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L))=0$ for $n<a-c$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; elementary support calculation using its product formula.

proof.text: In the lower-cohomology case the same definition gives $\operatorname{Hom}^n_R(Q,J)=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q^p,J^{p+n})$. If $n>b-c$, then for $p\ge c$ we have $p+n\ge c+n>b$, whence $J^{p+n}=0$; for $p<c$ we have $Q^p=0$. Again every factor and hence the product are zero, and its degree-$n$ cohomology is zero. Step 3 gives $H^n(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L))=0$ for $n>b-c$. Throughout, $a,b$ are the fixed support bounds of the original $J$; only the truncations depend on $K,c$. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis entered either calculation.
